title: Axonal Proteome Analysis and Western Blot via APEX2 Labeling
author: Chuyu Chen
materials: Tissue lysis buffer recipe: 50 mM Tris (pH 8.0), 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X-100, 5 mM Trolox, 10 mM sodium ascorbate, 10 mM sodium azide, and Halt protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

Determining protein concentration of frozen tissue lysates using the BCA assay (Thermo Scientific) 10 μg APEX2 labeled tissue lysate (from step 12) was loaded into 4–12% NuPAGE Bis-Tris PAGE (Invitrogen) as input.
Immediately placed the beads onto a magnetic rack and the entire sample was immediately loaded into 4–12% NuPAGE Bis-Tris PAGE (Invitrogen)

Incubate the membranes with primary antibodies specific for streptavidin-HRP (1:1000, Abcam), LRRK2/Dardarin clone N137/6 (1:1000, NeuroMab), Th (1:1000, Millipore), Rab3a (1:1000, Sigma), Rab3c (1:1000, Proteintech) overnight at 4°C
Chemiluminescent blots were imaged using the iBright imaging system (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Peptide concentrations in mass spectrometry ready samples were measured using the mBCA assay (Thermo Scientific Pierce).

For DIA LC-MS/MS measurements, peptides were injected on an in-house packed reversed phase column on a Thermo Scientific EASY-nLC 1200 nano-liquid chromatography system connected to a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer equipped with a Nanospray Flex ion source and a FAIMS Pro ion mobility device (Thermo Scientific).

steps.title: Anesthetize and perfuse mice
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice with ketamine and perform transcardial perfusion using 10 mL of ice‑cold cutting solution saturated with 95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare cutting solution
steps.instruction: Make cutting solution containing 110 mM choline, 2.5 mM KCl, 1.25 mM NaH₂PO₄, 10 mM glucose, 7 mM MgCl₂, 0.5 mM CaCl₂, 1.3 mM NaH₂PO₄, and 25 mM NaHCO₃; keep ice‑cold and O₂/CO₂‑saturated.

steps.title: Extract brain and slice
steps.instruction: Quickly extract the brain, place it in ice‑cold cutting solution (95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂), and cut coronal slices 300 µm thick using a Leica VT1200S vibratome.

steps.title: Incubate slices in biotin‑phenol aCSF
steps.instruction: Transfer slices to a glass dish containing artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) supplemented with 0.5 mM biotin‑phenol; continuously saturate with 95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂ and incubate 60 min at room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Add H₂O₂ for labeling
steps.instruction: Add 1 mM H₂O₂ directly to the aCSF containing the slices, incubate 5 min at RT.

steps.title: Quench labeling
steps.instruction: Rapidly transfer slices to a separate glass dish with quenching aCSF (aCSF + 10 mM Trolox, 20 mM sodium ascorbate, 10 mM sodium azide) and incubate 5 min at RT.

steps.title: Dissect and freeze tissue
steps.instruction: Rapidly dissect the slices in ice‑cold quenching aCSF, flash‑freeze the collected tissue on dry ice, and store at –80 °C until downstream processing.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize frozen APEX2‑labeled tissue in 0.75 mL ice‑cold tissue lysis buffer on ice using a glass Dounce homogenizer (30 strokes with pestle A followed by 30 strokes with pestle B).

steps.title: Add SDS and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 39 µL of 10 % SDS to achieve a final SDS concentration of 0.5 %, then incubate on a rotary wheel for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 21 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect supernatant for precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a pre‑chilled Eppendorf tube; for LC‑MS proceed to TCA precipitation, for western blot store at –80 °C.

steps.title: TCA precipitation
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold 55 % trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to the supernatant, incubate on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Acetone wash of pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the resulting protein pellet in 1 mL pre‑chilled (‑20 °C) acetone.

steps.title: Resuspend in Urea Dissolve Buffer
steps.instruction: Remove residual acetone and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL Urea Dissolve Buffer (8 M urea, 1 % SDS, 100 mM sodium phosphate pH 8, 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate).

steps.title: Sonicate and agitate
steps.instruction: Sonicate the suspension for 1 min, then place on an orbital shaker for gentle agitation for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Aliquot and dilute sample
steps.instruction: Take a 5 % aliquot of the resuspended protein, flash‑freeze and store at –80 °C. Dilute the remaining 95 % with water to reach a final concentration of 4 M urea and 0.5 % SDS.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend streptavidin magnetic beads (Thermo Fisher #88817) at 0.5 mg per 50 mL in ice‑cold Urea Detergent Wash Buffer (4 M urea, 0.5 % SDS, 100 mM sodium phosphate pH 8).

steps.title: Incubate beads with protein
steps.instruction: Add the prepared beads to each protein sample, place tubes on a magnetic stand for 1 min, then incubate overnight on a rotary wheel at 4 °C for 14–18 h.

steps.title: Wash beads in Urea Detergent Buffer
steps.instruction: Wash beads three times with 1 mL Urea Detergent Wash Buffer for 15 min each at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 1 mL Urea Detergent Wash Buffer, incubate 15 min at 4 °C, place on magnetic stand, discard supernatant. Repeat two more times.

steps.title: Wash beads in Urea Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Wash beads three times with 1 mL Urea Wash Buffer (4 M urea, 100 mM sodium phosphate pH 8) for 10 min each at RT.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 1 mL Urea Wash Buffer, incubate 10 min at RT, place on magnetic stand, discard supernatant. Repeat two more times.

steps.title: Elute biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in ~20 µL 1× SDS sample buffer supplemented with 20 mM DTT and 2 mM biotin, then boil for 5 min at 95 °C to elute bound proteins.

steps.title: SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Separate eluted proteins by NuPAGE SDS‑PAGE, then transfer to nitrocellulose membranes using the iBlot system (Invitrogen).

steps.title: Membrane blocking and primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash membranes three times with TBS‑Tween‑20 (10 min each), block as appropriate, incubate with primary antibody (as used in the study) overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate membranes with secondary anti‑mouse or anti‑rabbit antibody (1:2000, Thermo Scientific) for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Chemiluminescent detection
steps.instruction: Incubate membranes with Immobilon ECL Ultra Western HRP Substrate (Millipore) for 3 min and image the signal.

steps.title: In‑solution trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Solubilize the remaining protein sample in urea‑containing denaturation buffer and digest overnight with sequencing‑grade trypsin (Promega). Each digest corresponds to the eluted proteins from one mouse.

steps.title: Collect beads and clean‑up supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect beads on a magnetic rack, transfer the supernatant to a new tube for downstream peptide clean‑up.

steps.title: Peptide purification
steps.instruction: Purify peptides using an Oasis HLB μElution Plate (30 µm, Waters) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Dry and reconstitute peptides
steps.instruction: Dry peptides to complete dryness in a SpeedVac, then dissolve in LC solvent A (1 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid in water) containing Biognosys iRT‑peptide mix for retention‑time calibration.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Perform LC‑MS/MS using a gradient of solvent B (80 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % FA) from 1 % to 50 % over 171 min, followed by 90 % B for 7 min, then re‑equilibrate at 1 % B for 0.5 column volumes at 64 °C. Flow rate ramps from 450 nL/min at start to 271 nL/min at 172 min (wash at 400 nL/min).

steps.title: DIA data analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze DIA data with Spectronaut (Biognosys, v19.0); set peptide‑ and protein‑level false discovery rate (FDR) to 1 %.

steps.title: Database search parameters
steps.instruction: Search against a mouse UniProt FASTA (2024‑07‑01) allowing up to 2 missed cleavages; set carbamidomethylation of cysteine as fixed modification and variable modifications including N‑terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, deamidation (N/Q), and phosphorylation (S/T/Y) (up to 5 per peptide).

steps.title: HRM data analysis
steps.instruction: Process HRM data in Spectronaut (v19.0) with 1 % FDR, apply row‑based extraction, and normalize using global median normalization with the directDIA+ library generated in this project.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Perform two‑sample Student’s t‑tests on protein or phosphosite intensities; consider candidates with p‑value ≤ 0.58 and fold‑change > 1.5. Generate heat maps (Manhattan distance, Ward.D clustering) and PCA (prcomp in R). Conduct functional enrichment with STRING‑db (v12.0).
